reforms.description: The Omnibus Trade and Competitiveness Act of 1988 established programmes to accelerate technology transfer from R&D to industry, including regional centres providing direct support to small and medium-sized manufacturing firms for automation and modernisation. The Act created a National Advisory Committee on Semiconductors and mandated a national commission on Superconductivity to ensure U.S. leadership in semiconductor and superconducting technology development and application.
reforms.package_name: Omnibus Trade and Competitiveness Act of 1988
reforms.component_name: Commercialising R&D — technology transfer centres and sectoral commissions
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Technology transfer programmes and sectoral focus on semiconductors and superconductivity support commercialisation of R&D, raising productivity and competitive advantage in high-value sectors.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'established' and 'created' in past tense, and explicitly notes 'legislated' status; Act passed in 1988.
reforms.importance_rationale: Omnibus legislation establishing multiple technology transfer mechanisms and sectoral advisory bodies represents a structural, system-wide policy intervention.
reforms.source_quote: A significant proportion of the Trade Act (the Omnibus Trade and Competitiveness Act) addresses the issue of improving the commercialisation of U.S. R&D effort. New programmes are directed at the rapid transfer of technology to industry, via regional centres intended to provide direct support to small and medium-sized manufacturing firms.

reforms.description: The text identifies insufficient investment in commercial R&D as a structural impediment to U.S. productivity performance and calls for correction through broader microeconomic policy focused on resource allocation rather than selective industrial targeting.
reforms.package_name: Microeconomic Policy Reform for R&D Investment
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing commercial R&D investment raises productivity and innovation capacity; emphasis on resource allocation efficiency supports allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: Text presents this as a policy position or recommendation ('needs to be corrected') without evidence of legislative action or implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a policy recommendation or diagnostic statement about the need for reform, not a concrete implemented or legislated reform. No specific instrument or programme is described.
reforms.source_quote: There remain a number of general structural impediments to better productivity performance, such as low savings and the associated high cost of capital, and insufficient investment in general education, skill development and commercial R&D, which need to be corrected.
